title: What stays when five negative tokens leave seven?
description: Seven negative tokens sit in a pile and five of them are taken away. The tokens that stay are negative. Keeko thinks the answer is bigger because he adds the seven and the five.
teaching_notes: One idea: taking negative tokens away from negative tokens leaves fewer negative tokens, and the sign stays negative. Watch for students who put the two numbers together instead of taking one away from the other.

video_script.why: The child subtracts negative tokens from negative tokens by taking them away and sees that the pile gets smaller.
video_script.substitution: Lift the negative tokens being subtracted off the pile and read the answer from the negative tokens that stay.
video_script.wrong_move: puts the seven and the five together instead of taking five tokens away from the pile of seven
video_script.payoff_line: Negative seven take away negative five leaves negative two.
maths_rules: (−7) means 7 negative tokens; (−5) means 5 negative tokens
take away 5 of the 7 negative tokens
slip: 7 + 5 = 12 puts the tokens together; subtraction takes tokens away
video_script.design: One idea: take the negative tokens away from the pile and read the answer from the tokens that stay. Negative tokens are red as in the book. Keeko's doubt is that the seven and the five are put together.

<bookmark mark='fix'/>Taking tokens away makes the pile smaller, so it cannot grow to twelve red tokens.
